simple.meaning: אֹרְחָה (ʼôrᵉchâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a caravan.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 37:25. The surrounding context includes Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֹרְחָה (H736) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: אֹרְחָה (ʼôrᵉchâh) / H736 is traced through Genesis 37:25, Isaiah 21:13 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H736. orechah [ אֹרְחָה ] noun feminine travelling company, caravan (strictly Participle of אָרַח ), construct אֹרְחַת Gen 37:25 ; plural construct אֹרְחוֺת Isa 21:13 ; compare also below אֹרַח , 4 אֲרִיאֵיל אֲרִיאֵל, etc., see I. & II. ארה .

occurrences.englishText: They sat down to eat bread, and they lifted up their eyes and looked, and saw a caravan of Ishmaelites was coming from Gilead, with their camels bearing spices and balm and myrrh, going to carry it down to Egypt.
